identity.title: VTE risk history (Wells items): immobilization >=3 days or surgery within 4-12 weeks, prior objectively confirmed VTE, active malignancy

technique.how: Ask directly: bed rest >=3 days or major surgery within the past 4-12 weeks; any previous DVT or PE confirmed by imaging; cancer treated within 6 months or palliative. Record each item separately for the Wells DVT or PE score rather than as a global impression.
technique.prerequisites: Patient or collateral historian able to give a reliable history; check the chart for prior imaging-confirmed VTE and oncology history.

interpretation.positive_finding: Any single risk factor raises the probability of DVT only modestly (pooled LR+ about 1.8-2.7); the value comes from combining items in a Wells score, where a high score carries LR ~5.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of individual risk factors does not exclude VTE; a low Wells score (LR ~0.25) plus a negative D-dimer is what allows exclusion without imaging.
interpretation.pitfalls: Risk-factor LRs were pooled from heterogeneous cohorts and are weaker in patients with prior VTE. Malignancy and prior VTE also raise D-dimer, so they do not license D-dimer-only exclusion in high-probability patients.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive items push the Wells score toward moderate/high: order compression ultrasound (or CTPA) rather than relying on D-dimer alone; negative items lower the score and enable D-dimer exclusion.

sources.citation: Goodacre S, Sutton AJ, Sampson FC. Meta-analysis: The value of clinical assessment in the diagnosis of deep venous thrombosis. Ann Intern Med. 2005;143(2):129-139.
Wells PS, Owen C, Doucette S, Fergusson D, Tran H. Does this patient have deep vein thrombosis? JAMA. 2006;295(2):199-207.
Chunilal SD, Eikelboom JW, Attia J, et al. Does this patient have pulmonary embolism? JAMA. 2003;290(21):2849-2858.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use individual risk factors alone to exclude VTE; do not apply Wells-based D-dimer exclusion to inpatients, pregnant patients, or those already anticoagulated, where the derivation cohorts do not apply.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Hypotension, syncope or hypoxia with any VTE risk factor mandates immediate imaging or empiric anticoagulation, not D-dimer triage.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Wells items are defined explicitly to reduce interobserver variation, but Goodacre 2005 reports substantial heterogeneity across cohorts for individual features.

extraction_notes: Individual-item LRs come from the Goodacre 2005 Ann Intern Med meta-analysis abstract (no CIs, no sens/spec reported in abstract; full text not open access, so CIs left null). JAMA RCE 2006 (Wells) and 2003 (Chunilal) abstracts report only category-level prevalence, not per-item LRs; RCE 2006 entered as a prevalence-only estimate. PE-specific per-item LRs could not be located in an accessible abstract; PE-side accuracy is inferred from the same Wells items and is not separately quantified here.
